questions.subject: ANTHROPOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: examine artifact using anthropological evidence

stimulus.body: A dig yields a ground stone axe, a broken pot, and a bone awl, each made or modified by human hands.

questions.stem: Which statement about artifact is best supported by the account?

An artifact is any natural object found at a site, including pebbles and shells that humans never touched.

options.text: An artifact is a written document recovered during excavation, such as a letter or a contract.
options.misconception: It expands the term to untouched natural objects, which are not artifacts.

options.text: An artifact is a feature such as a wall or hearth that cannot be removed from the site.
options.misconception: It narrows the term to writing, excluding the great majority of archaeological finds.

questions.explanation: It confuses an artifact with a feature, which is a non-portable remain.
questions.hint: Artifacts are the portable material traces of past human action.

questions.subject: ANTHROPOLOGY
questions.learningObjective: examine lithic technology using anthropological evidence

options.text: Lithic technology is the dating of a site by the radioactive decay of minerals.
options.misconception: It assigns the term to faunal analysis, which uses animal remains.

questions.explanation: It assigns the term to dating, which is a chronological method.
questions.hint: Stone tools preserve well and record sequences of decisions about raw material and technique.

questions.subject: ANTHROPOLOGY

questions.subject: ANTHROPOLOGY
